steps.text: Midday. The skies are clear, as though the heavy rains the night before had been nothing but a lie.
The second tallest of Shangshu's Three Mounts is Mount Juqi. Juqi is home to only two of the Seventeen Peaks, the lesser of which is Nini Peak.
There are twenty two hundred and twenty two steps leading up to Nini Peak. While this may seem like a fascinating coincidence, additional steps were added specifically for the gimmick.
The steps lead heavenward through the clouds. The higher you get, the fewer visitors can be found. A lush, green mountain, rarely ever trodden by footsteps.
A few men can be seen here and there; all of them appear to be pole-carriers on first glance.

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: This is no Mount T'ien, but truly, what a fine summit.

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: How do you suppose they built a teahouse up here in the mountains, when the roads aren't so much as paved?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: Hmm. By hand. How else?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: On our way up here, we saw a pole-carrier walking down the mountain, didn't we? They do this every day, carrying anything from foodstuffs to bricks up from the base of the mountain.

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: From what I hear, a single trip takes them a good few hours. It's very toilsome work. Even today, some remote mountains still rely on pole-carriers for their survival...

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: Can't they build a ropeway for some cable cars or something?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: First they'd need a plot of land to build it on, wouldn't they?

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: Right, not that I know the first thing about building ropeways... Those guys really are amazing, though.

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: They probably rake in quite a bit dough, don't they?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: Not until recently. I saw on the news not too long ago that the Shangshu magistrate thinks very highly of the coolies. The government's even footing the bill for the teahouses' tea... Uhh?

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Pardon... 'Scuse me.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Noon tea.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: You got it, Master Shang.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: Haven't seen you for a couple days. How've you been?

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Same old.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: What were you up to?

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Saw my son.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: Oh... It's that time again... I'd forgotten.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: If you'd told me sooner, we could've gone together.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Don't worry about it...

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: He likes it quiet.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: *Sigh*... It's been years now... I'm only saying this because we know each other so well, and I mean no disrespect, but well...

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: We can't be stuck in the past.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: You speaking for Zheng Qingyue?

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: Come on, you know he personally invested in all the teahouses here.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: You're on his payroll. You speak for him. No offense taken.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: That's half my own opinion too.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Half-offended then.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: It's been years already. Just hear me out.

steps.name: Teahouse Assistant
steps.text: Have some tea and think it through.

steps.name: Teahouse Stopperby
steps.text: Isn't that the man we saw go down the mountain earlier...?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: I-I think so? It hasn't been that long, has it? He's back already?

steps.name: Teahouse Tourist
steps.text: He and his buddies must have some kind of relay system so he only has to go down halfway. That's the only plausible explanation.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: No good... Can't get through to 'em.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: There's no response, which means Nian and Dusk aren't in Shangshu yet... They might not be following the mission directives.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Yeah, I know what you're about to say.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: I'm hardly a clever man, and I certainly can't claim to remember everything I see, but if my eyes did not deceive me...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: The case that Mr. Lee handed to Mr. Liang... carried the same pattern as the trinket that Nian had.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Must have something to do with them suddenly breaking off from the team.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: What should we do?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hm... Well, I kind of saw this coming too.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I talked to Lava, you see. Asked her to contact the Operators near Shangshu and have them come get us as soon as she made it to the office.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh? So you came prepared?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nian was acting awfully dodgy the whole way. I figured she was up to something.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Are you suggesting we stay here for the time being then?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: We bumped into Mr. Lee. Naturally we have to help him. It's in the contract and everything.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: I see. You'll handle this fairly and impartially, while remaining vigilant and conscientious. You continue to command my utmost respect, benefactor.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: But Mr. Lee's a smart man... He never bothered requesting Rhodes Island's assistance ever since we ran into him at the inn. Maybe he's been trying to tell us not to get involved.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: If this really does have to do with Nian, though... Not to mention Taihe and Zuo Le...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Anyway, we'll check out the rendezvous point when the time comes. Nian's probably gonna be a no-show, but Dusk isn't that kind of girl. We might see her there.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Right. Dusk is likely to drop a hint or two, at least.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: No matter how I slice it, though, sometimes things are just too—

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: —Too coincidental?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Nothing, mate, you didn't have any particular reason for choosing that inn, right?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh, you jest. Suppose I had an ulterior motive, how could I have counted on a Gloompincer knocking my car over and then us running into each other?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Then just who is it that made everything line up so perfectly?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor... that WAS a jest, right? A joke, a jape? You couldn't possibly be suspecting me, could you? Benefactor?!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: What's the matter...?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I thought I was in charge of this whole thing?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Someone has to clean up the mess.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: If you can do it, then clearly I could too—

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Wrong.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Even if you could, you can't. As long as you're still Du Yaoye and not Du, Head of the Escort Association, there is absolutely no way.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Why?!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Do you still fail to realize why I didn't seize the target when he was at the inn? Why I stopped you, even?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: It was because of that Cautus with the skills, and that Nothing dude—

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: It seems you still have much to learn.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: What do you mean...?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: You have no eye for people.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Do you want me to inherit the Association, or do you want me to be the naive Miss Du my whole life?!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: An escort has many enemies. You don't understand.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And so I should continue to be the stupid, ignorant daughter of the Association's head?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I'm supposed to let everyone think that Zheng, Head of the Escort Association, is now just an honest businessman, and I'm a successor who's not up to snuff?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: You know that's not who I am.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Ye, my girl...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Do you know the size of the bone the young people at the Escort Association have to pick with you?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: What do they know?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And what do you know?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: You're trying to wash your hands of the business, yet you don't even realize how long the younger generation has been unhappy with the current state of the Association.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Then are you telling me, in all honesty, that starting a new association with those inexperienced disciples is what you truly want?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Is that who you are now?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: All I know is that you made me do this, Dad. And that if I succeed, not only will they all bow down to me, I'll have a fine new addition to my rap sheet.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: I'm worried that you might not have what it takes.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: And I'm even more worried that you're actually trying to mess this up.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I don't know what you're talking about...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: If you've changed your mind, then hurry up and tell me. And if you haven't, then...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Stop worrying about me.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: How did it go, Miss...? What did the innkeeper say?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Hmph, how do you think it went?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Zheng got played. They switched it out with a decoy.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: At least we don't have to screw this one up ourselves. Sounds like he's already on top of it.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Not necessarily.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: He knows what we're up to.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: H-Huh?

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: He knows? What should we do, then? If our masters ground us, we can't do nothing!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Solving a problem like this can take a while, but creating a new one is simple enough.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I had this same thought when I first visited Shangshu years ago, but the people here are really quite something.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: From Xinluan to Liuyun, how many wondrous peaks and precipitous paths will we have to cross? The city is dispersed along the mountain chain, and there are settlements scattered all across. What a wondrous sight.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: So... have you come to understand why you came to be robbed?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm not stupid.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Though I trust Liang Xun, and therefore I trust you, Master Shen.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: *Sigh*... Well, you've got smarts, I'll give you that.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Is that what Liang Xun said about me?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: I came to that conclusion myself. Where does Mr. Liang come into this?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: He once told me that I put up a front and my predictions never come true, but I have a good eye for people.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: That's what I meant.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It's all a matter of experience.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Let's go. This is as high as Huntan Peak gets, and we haven't seen any pavilions on our way up here.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Qujiang Peak isn't far from here, but why pick that one? If we're looking for someone, shouldn't we start where more people live?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What did they used to call Qujiang?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Zuanjiang Peak. It was difficult to write, so they changed it when it got turned into a tourist spot.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Bingo.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I had a dream that I was looking for someone on the peak.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Now if that isn't strange... Sure you didn't learn about the old name on your last trip to Shangshu?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Maybe... Or perhaps...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: ...I have a mountain spirit guiding me.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: You know how to use Arts, right?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Think they call 'em Originium Arts now? An inkhorn of a name, I tell you, but they've always been around, and may as well be the gods and spirits you speak of.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Now that's not quite right, Master Shen. It is man who uses Fulu, and thus it is man who triumphs over nature.

steps.name: Lee?
steps.text: 'It is man who triumphs over nature'?

steps.name: Lee?
steps.text: I think I like that saying.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Alright, alright. Originium Arts it is. I don't really get these Originium studies... Hm? What are you spacing out for?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Did I... Did I just say something...?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: 'Man who triumphs over nature'?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Never mind... I was probably daydreaming.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Qujiang Peak... Zuanjiang Peak.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: We looked there numerous times, but the search always came up emptyhanded.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Yet the Sui Regulator has nonetheless come to a decision.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Has her presence in Shangshu all these years ever proven to be a transgression, though?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Why, then, did she lend Yan her strength, defending her borders dozens of times?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Over such a long stretch of time, it certainly defies common sense.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: But the situation at hand seems to be going against your wishes, Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: If she is a shadow, then the goblet from Lungmen must be a flicker of light.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Did the light come first, or did the shadow? A difficult, yet meaningless question.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: What is truly difficult are the people who try to answer this question.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The Sui Regulator came to me directly, to reason with me in person. Naturally, I understand the gravity of the circumstances.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: You promised General Zuo that when the cup arrived in Shangshu, you would feign its theft, allowing it to make its way to his son, Lord Zuo.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: All to fool certain individuals.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Though I couldn't possibly have explained this all to Old Lee, an outsider.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Then you should not have chosen a Lungmenite to handle this.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Given my status, I can't act rashly. It would do more harm than good if it blemishes the early spring festivities.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: And as the magistrate, all matters, both large and small, are of the utmost importance to me.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Is he not a friend of yours?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: He is my friend, but he is also an outsider.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: We can hardly blame you, there are too many eyes.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: What of the cup?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: As I entrusted my friend with the matter, naturally it is with him.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: You wish to have the Lungmenite uncover Ling's whereabouts without lifting a finger yourself?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Rumor has it that the cup can possess the things around it. Is it true?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Mr. Taihe... I have a question myself.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Please, go ahead.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Let us cast aside our status and speak as equals.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The Sui Regulator bypassed the Ministry of Rites for this matter, far overstepping its bounds. Once the Ministry learns of this, there will likely be quite the quarrel between the two parties.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You are the Deputy Monitor Censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision. What are your thoughts?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I am indebted to the general, and I am merely repaying the favor.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It comes down to personal feelings, then?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: That is correct.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The Department of Discipline and Supervision's Monitor Censor oversees hundreds of officers and champions integrity. It seems to me there should be no place for personal feelings.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: If the Department of Discipline and Supervision learns of this and finds the Ministry of Rites in the right and the Sui Regulator in the wrong, what will become of those personal feelings?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Garner loyalty and forsake righteousness.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: There wasn't even the slightest hesitation in your answer, Mr. Taihe.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: It was the general himself who taught me those words.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Truly a fine man, then.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: You needn't worry, however.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: General Zuo is a Yanese soldier. He would never do anything illegal.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Did something force the Sui Regulator's hand, then? Even if it means bypassing the Ministry of Rites?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Right... Lord Exorcist Zuo Xuanliao is a man who normally gives the affairs in the borderlands his utmost attention. Who could have diverted his attention to a mere goblet?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: It's no trivial matter, but hardly a significant one either.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: And I am certain you already know who it is.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *sharp exhale*

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Please take care, Mr. Liang.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It seems this spring will be colder than expected.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Here we are.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Aside from a few houses here and there, this is the only town near Quijiang Peak.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What kind of place is this?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Before Shangshu City was built, it was near the border. The mountain was full of mineral resources, and many blacksmiths and stonemasons worked here.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What about now?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: With the world at peace, the nomadic cities are all parked around the mountain range. Aside from the few forges kept around as tourist spots, the town is mostly bed-and-breakfasts now.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: What lies at the top of Qujiang Peak, then...?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm... Perhaps just a place for wine and chess?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: After all, if it were scenic, there'd be no need to go look for them. Most likely it's a remote place no one ever visits.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: I know Shangshu's mounts and waters like the back of my hand... Never heard of any pavilions off the beaten path though.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Qujiang Peak has only an empty swath of land. The legend goes that a god, staring into the deep waters there, attained enlightenment by forgetting the waters surrounding it. From then on, everyone called it the 'Field of Forgotten Water.'

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sounds like our friend won't be easy to find, then... How about we start with the wine shops? Might be futile without knowing what they look like though.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Any ideas, Master Shen?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: When seeking a man, there is this one simple trick that has worked since ancient times.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Have them seek you out instead.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: True, but a little passive for my tastes.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I have an idea, though—

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: Need something?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Reading for leisure, I see. Fine tastes as always, my lord.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Reading for leisure enriches the mind.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: If there is something you would like to ask, please go ahead.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My lord, is something weighing on your mind?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Hm... What do you mean?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Your friend from Lungmen.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: There's no hiding anything from you, Miss Ning. There is a minor matter, though it's entirely personal.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: What does it concern?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: We are looking for someone.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Hm... What kind of someone?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: An old friend of ours. A practitioner of the martial arts.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I see. Is that all?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: His name is Huai.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: It seems a simple thing.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I did say it was a minor matter... You needn't worry.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You should hide no secrets from me, my lord.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: And I have none to hide.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Very well, then.
The lady before him walks across the room and takes a glance at the bookshelf. She appears engulfed in a sense of defeat.
Fortunately, her mood quickly lightens.
It often changes rapidly.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My lord, the book you were reading... Is it a historical record?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It's about an old Catastrophe that happened within the bounds of Shangshu's Three Mounts.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You seem to be very fond of that piece of history.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I saw it with my own eyes. I can never forget it.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: If I remember correctly... 'Tale of the Three Mounts?'

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'm surprised you remember. It seems I've reread that book far too many times.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I only happened to notice.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: May I borrow it? I will be paying Uncle Bai a visit. I can read it in my down time.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: As you wish.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Very well... But...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Oh, forgive me...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Let me get it for you. I haven't been able to read it much lately, so I placed it fairly high on the shelf.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: So you'll be visiting Bai, the potter?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Please give him my regards.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I will take my leave now.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tale of the Three Mounts...'

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My lord, I am sure you never realized, but I have actually already taken a peek at your bookshelf, once when you worked late into the night and fell asleep in your study.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: (He's never put this book so high up...)

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: (There was a new case on the shelf too... What could be inside?)
